q1_issues.issue: The answer conjunct (Member $x $c) is left wholly unconstrained, so it unifies with the query's own restrictors and returns ebb and deep — the terms the question already supplies — rather than an identifying class.

q2_gaps: identity / definition question ("What is the N?"): the Queries section covers role, attribute, time, measure and capability questions but never says what an "X is what?" question should ask for — which storage the answer variable ranges over (a Member/Inheritance class slot, a KindProperty, a definitional gloss), or how to keep that variable from matching the restrictors that identify the referent
review.notes: "deep ebb" is queried split (kind ebb + property deep) rather than as a fused kind, which the adjective+noun rule's incidental-description bar supports, though if the phrase is a term of art stored as deep_ebb this query would find nothing.

issues.reason: The observation is right that the open (Member $x $c) also unifies with the query's own restrictors, but 'rather than an identifying class' overstates it — an unconstrained class-slot answer variable is exactly the licensed shape of 'What does Bob do?' → (Member $e $verb) in Queries, no rule bars it, and any genuine identifying class still binds alongside the noise.

gaps_confirmed: no identity/definition question form: Queries covers role, attribute, time, measure and capability asks but never says what storage a 'What is the N?' answer variable ranges over, nor how to keep it from re-binding the restrictors that identify the referent
new_gaps: a query over a modifier+noun NP has no dual-storage union: the statement may have stored 'the deep ebb' fused (deep_ebb, a term of art) or split (ebb + deep per the incidental-description bar), and Core patterns' dual-storage list names no fused-compound/split-modifier pair, so the query must guess one storage and silently misses the other

a 'What is the N?' query must also guess whether the referent is stored as an individual (Member) or as a kind (Inheritance): a definite NP in a lore corpus is routinely the subject of a definitional Inheritance claim, and nothing licenses unioning the two branches
adjudication.notes: A query asserts nothing, so nothing false or ill-typed is emitted; the imprecision is entirely a property of the query language the reviewer correctly reported as a gap.
